explain.machine: Reciprocating piston block with crank drive - reading

steps.title: Machine Reading Overview
steps.text: My reading is this is a reciprocating pump or compressor block with spring loaded pistons and linkage drive. The section shows multiple bores side by side with rods and springs acting along a common axis. This interpretation is my reading from the hatched section and clustered parts.

steps.title: Frame Housing Support
steps.text: The heavy hatched body forms the housing that holds everything together. Side walls and back plates enclose the bores while leaving the drive side open for linkage. The block reads as rigid with bores aligned in parallel.

steps.title: Power Input Crank
steps.text: Power appears to enter through the large transverse shaft and crank on the open side. Rotation of the crank swings the connected links and pivot bosses to drive the inner rods. The large shaft looks substantially larger in proportion than the inner rods.

steps.title: Gears Passing Motion
steps.text: Motion is passed on through small gears with 17 teeth and 15 teeth beside the main wheel. The pairing of these gears was guessed because the section does not show clear meshing and tooth counts were guessed. The ratio is unknown because the teeth were not counted.

steps.title: Output Piston Motion
steps.text: The end motion is reciprocation of the pistons and rods within the bores. The small piston measures 5.6 mm in diameter at model scale, real size unknown, and moves with its spring and long rod. Springs return the pistons while links constrain sideways motion.

steps.title: Guessed Details Added
steps.text: Thicknesses and depths of plates and frames were guessed because the drawing gives only outlines in section. Lengths of pins through the walls were also guessed where hidden, and shafts and bearings were added by the engineer to support wheels and gears. A base block was added because the frame would not stand without support.
